January 2017–December 2025: 108 months. The public release ends in 2025, so Fund X’s 2026 observations do not enter benchmark comparisons.
195 strategies have complete common-period returns. Publication years are no later than 2016; original reported samples end no later than 2014.
194 of the same strategies also have complete 2005–2016 calibration data. DivOmit is excluded; exactly the same names enter the value-weighted comparison.
1980–2004 December-end windows. At 108 months: 3,148 eligible strategy-windows across 193 strategies and 17 endpoints. DelDRC has no complete development window.
2005–2016, before the 2017–2025 evaluation. Every reported K enters the common selection-reference cutoff.
2017–2025 is held out from map and cutoff fitting. Retrospective data revisions and catalogue selection remain.
Original-paper sorts and original weighting: some sorts are equal-weighted and some value-weighted. The matched forced-value version changes weighting only.
Source percent returns are divided by 100 once. Long-short means long-leg return minus short-leg return. It is already a zero-investment payoff; do not subtract cash again.
Cash return + one unit of long-short payoff per unit collateral: $1 long and $1 short, gross stock notional 2. Source returns omit execution, borrowing and management costs.
Monthly excess Sharpe = mean excess payoff / sample SD of excess payoff. h = mean of the actual diagnostic series / its sample SD. They differ for Fund X and funded series.
Monthly intercept in US Fama–French three-factor regression. Long-short spread enters directly; funded and Fund X total returns enter net of cash. t statistics use HAC with 4 lags.
Bias ratio B > 2 or fitted-normal lower binomial tail p < 0.05. Combined means either rule. This Gaussian adaptation is not the original Bollen–Pool test.
Count of returns in [0,SD], divided by 1 plus count in [−SD,0). Losses are strictly negative; the +1 convention is retained throughout.
Expected negative months under a fitted normal, T × Phi(−h), minus observed negative months. Larger values mean fewer losses than that reference predicts.
C is the larger development-period empirical rank of B and D. These ranks are not p-values. A strict score > cutoff triggers an alert.
Empirical 95th percentile for K=1 in the joint calendar-block calibration resamples.
Largest empirical 95th percentile across K = 1, 5, 20, 50, 100, 194 in calibration. This is a finite conditional historical reference, not a universal 5% guarantee.
Uniformly choose K distinct strategies from the fixed panel and retain the highest historical excess Sharpe. Rank-j winner weight is C(N−j,K−1) / C(N,K).

Common calendar indices resample all strategies and cash together, in circular time blocks. Low/high are 2.5th/97.5th percentiles conditional on the source history; no exact confidence coverage is claimed.
Eligible underlying losses at most delta are replaced initially by a 0.05% gain. Permanent or 1-, 3-, 6-month recognition rules use separate payoff and log-NAV accounting.
No forced recognition in the last observation. Delayed gaps have a scheduled future settlement; the available evaluation sample supplies no actual economic return tail.
One designated altered candidate is included with K−1 unaltered candidates. Selection, selected-plus-alert, and alert-given-selection probabilities have separate denominators.
Symmetric causal filter: (1−lambda) × current + lambda × previous, lambda = 0.25, 0.50, 0.75. It moves gains and losses alike.
Equal-notional, inverse-volatility and capped maximum-Sharpe weights use 2005–2016 only. Added after individual results; no calibrated flags are claimed for these new combined strategies.
Responses of specified return screens to observed reconstructed stock strategies and explicitly added reporting changes.
Actual false accusations, real-world fraud detection, investor authentication and general fund-population error rates. The strategies share stocks and market months.

Fund X is a reported net fund return; source portfolios are gross stock-strategy payoffs. Individual strategies do not reach Fund X’s common-period h. No benchmark means were shifted to close this gap.
Excel recalculates displayed fractions and conditional probabilities from their saved components. Refitting scores, portfolio weights or resampling requires the accompanying analysis code.
